newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Plan for domestic Bezeq offer advances.
newsitem.headline: Plan for domestic Bezeq offer advances.

text.p: Israeli Communications Minister Limor Livnat has decided to move ahead with a proposal to float Bezeq Israel Telecom shares in Israel, the Communications Ministry said on Tuesday.

"In a discussion at the minister's office today...it was decided to move immediately forward with the Bezeq privatisation process and to take the required measures for the purpose of selling shares of the compamy in the Israel's capital market," the ministry said.
The decision marks a turnaround in the government's long-standing plan to conduct a global offering in Bezeq, Israel main telecommunications company. The state controls 76 percent of the shares.

Livni said the decision to make a domestic offering came after officials concluded that a global offering could not be done before the end of 1997. She said the government wanted to show progress was being made on a major privatisation before then.
Attending the meeting were Tsipi Livni, the head of the Government Corporations Authority, as well as officials from the Communications Ministry, the Treasury and Bezeq, the ministry said.
"We will sell as much as we can. We are not limiting ourselves," Livni said after the meeting. She estimated the maximum block that could be floated at one time was between five and 10 percent.
The ministry said the decision did not preclude making a global offering or reaching an agreement with Britain's Cable & Wireless.

"This process (of floating Bezeq domestically) will be done in parallel with continued intensive talks with Cable & Wireless and the preparation of the planned international offering," the ministry said.

Cable & Wireless acquired 10 percent of Bezeq in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange without the government's knowledge nearly two years ago. Since then, the two sides have been in talks over the company's future role in Bezeq.
A delegation from the British company is due to arrive in Israel this week for further talks, but Livni said the decision to proceed with a domestic offering was unrelated to the discussions.
On Monday, Livni told the daily newspaper Haaretz that floating Bezeq overseas would be more difficult than at home if the Cable & Wireless issue was not resolved.
